comment: Every rendered verdict on this page carries data-verdict="<id>" and every rendered
measurement carries data-claim="<id>". Each id below is killed by at least one
mutation recorded here: a single-token edit to real source that forces the measured
value the other way. A kill counts only when the unmutated baseline passed in the
same run and the failure is that marker's own assertion — not a build error, a blank
page, or the whole suite going red.
`kills` names, per marker, the TEST and the exact CLAIM that kills it. That is not
documentation: e2e/global-teardown.ts requires each of those to have been OBSERVED
executing. expectVerdict/expectClaim record every (test, marker, claim) they run, and
the rule is checked against that record rather than against the spec's source text.
The source form of this rule was defeated three ways across this lane — comment the
call out; keep it but feed it values read off the page; satisfy a file-granular rule
from an unrelated line elsewhere in the file — because a mention is not an assertion.
See e2e/observations.ts. There is no separate `covers` list: the keys of `kills` ARE
the covered set, so the two cannot disagree.
verdict-coverage.spec.ts fails if the page renders a marker of EITHER family that no
mutation covers, if a mutation names a marker the page never renders, or if a
mutation's `find` string no longer appears exactly once in its file (a rotted
mutation guards nothing). Run them with: node scripts/mutate.mjs apply <id>

claim.text: MATCH — both modules independently derived the same 32 bytes

session-key-match.test: session-key-match renders the byte-for-byte verdict, not a canned banner

session-key-state.test: session-key-state labels SK from the comparison, not the step counter

session-keys-match.why: Forces the one byte-for-byte comparison every SK verdict reads. All three surfaces must follow it.

adversary-model.test: adversary-model derives SK only when both assumptions are granted

kdf-input-state.test: kdf-input-state opens exactly the boxes the grant covers

adversary-keeps-kem-secret.why: Withholds the modeled lattice break. The panel must stop claiming SK OPENED and the SS box must stop reading OPENED IN MODEL.

alice-accepts-bad-pq-signature.find: throw new HandshakeAbort('Signed ML-KEM prekey signature verification failed')

prekey-signature-abort.test: prekey-signature-abort names the check that fired

claim.contains: ABORT — Signed ML-KEM prekey signature verification failed

alice-accepts-bad-pq-signature.why: Removes the authentication check the exhibit claims fires. The page must stop naming the rejection.

bob-accepts-failed-aead.replace: return { components, sessionKey, plaintext: new Uint8Array() }

kem-tamper-abort.test: kem-tamper-abort names the AEAD as the place the mismatch surfaced

claim.contains: REJECTED AT FIRST AEAD — Initial AEAD authentication failed after ML-KEM implicit rejection

bob-accepts-failed-aead.why: Accepts a forged tag. The tamper exhibit must stop reporting REJECTED AT FIRST AEAD.

last-resort-reuse.test: last-resort-reuse measures the three facts it claims

contains: Reuse does not reveal either SK by itself

bundle-mislabels-last-resort.why: Breaks one of the three facts the reuse verdict measures. SAME PQ KEY ID must not render.

impersonation.test: impersonation reports four measured checks, not a flag

impersonation-signer-check.why: Makes one of the four measured checks report FAIL. The headline must fall back to FIXTURE INVALID.

ratchet-heal.test: ratchet-heal reaches both outcomes from a chain that is always built

ratchet-grant-is-not-a-recovery.why: Hands the adversary a secret that is not the one behind the wire public key. The chain must stall and STILL READ must not render — this is the mutation the old tautological stillReadable could not fail.

ratchet-honest-updates.test: ratchet-heal reaches both outcomes from a chain that is always built

ratchet-count-ignores-the-chain.why: Takes the rendered update count off the chain it counts. That sentence read 'Three honest root updates completed' as an English literal while runRatchetModel built the chain from `step < 3`; an auditor rendered 'Seven honest root updates completed' over a four-root chain with the gate green at 25 passed, because the oracle asserted the chain's length, distinctness and anchor root and never read the count beside it. A chain of N roots is N-1 updates, and the oracle now compares the two.

ratchet-model-updates.test: ratchet-heal reaches both outcomes from a chain that is always built

ratchet-model-count-ignores-the-chain.why: The same edit on the adversary's chain. 'the curve-break model recomputed all three' was the other half of that English literal; with no model granted the classical observer recomputes zero, which the page now renders as a number rather than asserting in a clause.

wire-kem-ct-bytes.test: wire-kem-ct-bytes and wire-ad-bytes measure the message rather than restate it

wire-counts-the-aead-not-the-kem.why: Reports the AEAD ciphertext where the strip says KEM CT. The rendered 1,568 B must follow the ML-KEM ciphertext actually sent, not whichever byte string is nearest.

wire-secrecy.test: wire-secrecy searches the sent bytes rather than asserting they are clean

claim.contains: searched the sent bytes for all 192 bytes
claim.absent: SECRET BYTES FOUND ON THE WIRE

wire-secret-bytes.test: wire-secrecy searches the sent bytes rather than asserting they are clean

wire-search-matches-anything.why: Inverts the byte comparison the secret search rests on, so every secret 'appears' on the wire. NO SECRET ON THE WIRE must stop rendering and the found-bytes count must move off 0 — this is the mutation a hard-coded '0 B' could not fail.

wire-counts-secrets-not-their-bytes.find: const scannedSecretBytes = secrets.reduce((total, secret) => total + secret.length, 0)

wire-scanned-secret-bytes.test: wire-secrecy searches the sent bytes rather than asserting they are clean

wire-counts-secrets-not-their-bytes.why: Reports how many secrets were searched as though it were how many bytes. The anti-vacuity number beside 'found none' has to be the summed width of what was actually searched. The limit this exhibit cannot exceed is recorded beside the code: every secret here is 32 B, so summing them and multiplying one width by six are observationally identical, and `secrets.length * 32` would survive this suite.

wire-ad-bytes.test: wire-kem-ct-bytes and wire-ad-bytes measure the message rather than restate it

wire-ad-measures-only-the-x3dh-prefix.why: Measures only the two X25519 identity keys X3DH bound, dropping the ML-KEM public key PQXDH Revision 3 adds to AD. The AD size the page shows must be the length of the buffer the AEAD really authenticated. (An earlier form of this mutation deleted the associatedData read entirely; that failed `tsc` instead of the assertion, which is a build error and not a kill.)
